translations.answer: The project contributor confirmed only one project fact: the distillation phase did not add noise, and stated that the deployment was effective. The post did not explain why this is feasible, nor compare it with a noise-added configuration, so it can only be reused as a record for Human2Humanoid implementation and cannot be concluded that other robots do not need noise randomness.
translations.applicability: Limited to the distillation and deployment process described in this project report; missing version and sensor environment information.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication are missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author team completed the deployment with a distillation configuration without observation noise.
translations.details.environments.0: LeCAR-Lab/human2humanoid; distillation phase; specific commit and sensor configuration not mentioned.
translations.details.limits.0: No quantified results, control experiments, version, or applicable sensor range; cannot be generalized as 'no noise' in general.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The project contributor stated that the configuration runs well in their deployment.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why hasn't the Human2Humanoid strategy distilled model included observation noise?
translations.details.symptoms.0: Code reviewers found that the distilled observation was not explicitly noised.
translations.source.title: Human2Humanoid Distillation Phase Missing Observation Noise
translations.title: Human2Humanoid Should Observation Noise Be Added in Policy Distillation Phase?
